latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with (n-1)/n \le t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 \le k \le n. Since k>0, multiplying the inequality for t by k gives
k(n-1)/n \le kt < k.
Now k \le n implies k/n \le 1, so
k(n-1)/n = k - k/n \ge k-1.
Therefore k-1 \le kt < k. Because k-1 and k are consecutive integers, it follows that
floor(k t) = k-1.

In particular, taking k=n yields floor(nt)=n-1. Hence
E_n(t) = floor(nt) - \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{floor(k t)}{k}
= (n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k-1}{k}.
Writing \frac{k-1}{k}=1-\frac1k and using H_n := \sum_{k=1}^n \frac1k, we get
\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k-1}{k} = \sum_{k=1}^n \left(1-\frac1k\right) = n - H_n.
Therefore
E_n(t) = (n-1) - (n-H_n) = H_n - 1.
So for every such t, floor(k t)=k-1 for all 1\le k\le n, and hence E_n(t)=H_n-1.
role_in_parent: Exhibit the maximizing interval and compute the value there.
statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k-1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, and hence E_n(t) = H_n - 1.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n greater than 1
t is a real number satisfying (n-1)/n is at most t
t is a real number with t strictly less than 1
k is an integer with k at least 1
k is an integer with k at most n
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n greater than 1, for all real numbers t with (n-1)/n <= t and t < 1, and for all integers k with 1 <= k <= n, floor of (k times t) equals k minus 1; therefore E_n(t) equals H_n minus 1.
